style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: Clean isometric cutaway illustration of a residential water heater with a pressure-reducing valve and a steel thermal expansion tank on the cold-water copper inlet, drawn in thin graphite linework with one deep pine green accent, laid flat on a plywood workbench in a garage. Hard directional light from the left rakes across the paper, bone white and graphite and deep pine green, generous empty bench to the left, cutaway off-centre right, deep contact shadow under the paper. Matte vellum surface, drafting table texture, physical depth.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, legible numbers, logos
rationale: A technical isometric cutaway can diagram the exact physical relationship between the pressure-reducing valve, water heater, and expansion tank without needing legible numbers or labels, making a regulatory and mechanical relationship instantly readable. It also places the drawing on a garage workbench, matching the site's home environment.
subject: pressure-reducing valve and expansion tank on a residential water heater cold-water inlet
core_thesis: Static pressure above 80 psi mandates a pressure-reducing valve, which closes the system and makes an expansion tank on the water heater the second half of the job.
core_conflict: code-mandated pressure control versus closed-system thermal expansion
composition: extreme asymmetry with cutaway off-centre right

review.depicts: A printed sheet lying on a wooden surface bearing a technical isometric line drawing of a cylindrical water heater shown in cutaway with green water inside, connected by piping to a smaller domed expansion tank and a valve fitting on the inlet line to its left.
review.reason: The drawing depicts precisely the article's mechanism — a water heater with an expansion tank and pressure-reducing valve on the cold-water inlet — so a reader would recognize the story's subject.
